rationale: telecomm-adpcm is a tiny (933 text bytes, 4 functions) DSP benchmark whose hot code is the tight arithmetic loops in adpcm_coder and adpcm_decoder, so the table favors low-cost transforms (SUB, SPLIT, IGV) while restraining the size- and runtime-expensive ones: BCF gets high RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights (0.80/0.85) since bogus blocks would balloon a sub-1KB binary and sit in per-sample inner loops, and FLA keeps high SecurityGain (0.85) — flattening the two large decode/encode state machines yields the best reverse-engineering resistance per byte here — but with elevated RuntimeCost/SizeCost (0.70) so the feature selector applies it selectively to adpcm_coder/adpcm_decoder rather than main or _start. IGV is favored (SecurityGain 0.65, low costs) because this program's behavior pivots on static lookup tables (step-size/index tables) whose concealment disrupts pattern-matching deobfuscation cheaply; SUB gets strong DiversityGain to break signature matching with negligible overhead; IBR and ICALL sit in the middle as diversity multipliers with moderate costs, ICALL slightly penalized on CorrectnessRisk (0.40) because telecomm-adpcm has few call sites and added indirect-call plumbing risks ABI missteps in a target where correctness of the bitstream round-trip is paramount. No pass is fully omitted, preserving build-to-build diversity, but the cost weights ensure BCF/FLA fire only where function features justify them.
